requirement.summary: Atomic multi-seat Hold, database TTL, frozen price, exact total, and side-effect-free rejection.
Checkout preserves one frozen total and one provider identity through UNKNOWN and reconciliation.
Expiry releases only eligible Hold ownership while terminal Order ownership and immutable history remain.
FIFO entries choose one deterministic same-zone same-row strictly contiguous set without partial ownership.
Offer freezes every seat price for 120 seconds and accept, decline, cancel, and expiry close atomically.
Lost and concurrent Hold or checkout responses replay one persisted status, body, and semantic effect.
Overlapping multi-seat requests across APIs linearize without oversell or partial acquisition.
Equivalent external payment facts converge to one legal terminal payment, order, and seat history.
Concurrent releases preserve FIFO eligibility, one active Offer per Entry, and one live owner per Seat.
Accept, decline, cancel, and expiry race to one legal terminal result and at most one Hold.
SIGKILL after claim permits reclaim while stale work cannot release twice or lose terminal Work.
A persisted provider effect with an unknown response recovers through the original identity after worker death.
Killed matching or expiry workers are reclaimed without duplicate Offer, owner, or expired Entry revival.
Committed seat and payment events retry with stable identity, canonical body, and aggregate sequence.

requirement.summary: Runtime exposes exact V1 and Manager resource wires, strict inputs, stable errors, and tenant isolation.
Chromium uses visible controls and public HTTP to Hold, checkout, reconcile UNKNOWN, and refresh availability.

Create and cancel an Entry through real browser HTTP; check known Offer timer and frozen totals, with known-ID controls when available. No unprovided Entry/Offer discovery or refresh route is required.

requirement.summary: One authorized snapshot is exact, sorted, secret-free, and closes every live owner and frozen amount.

requirement.source: public policy learning-final-system-2026-09-08.1; current README and Manager requirements
requirement.summary: Current seat ownership, UNKNOWN payment and replay survive FINAL restart. Exercise only the current public API and legal seed on one FINAL submission; verify durable business state, identity and replay without historical binary, old database or synthetic migration-only wrappers.
Fifty thousand disjoint public Holds meet throughput and p95 while retaining post-load invariants.
Twenty thousand public attempts against one thousand Seats meet limits with exactly one live owner each.
Five thousand uncertain payments close within ninety seconds after two SIGKILLs and four replacements.
